# Deal Structure & Tax Planning — Step-Plan
**Project Codename:** [TARGET]
**Prepared by:** Redline Explainer / Deal Structuring Team
**Date:** October 3, 2026
**Version:** DRAFT v1.0 — PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL (Attorney–Client / Work Product)

---

## SECTION 1 — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This step-plan documents the recommended acquisition structure, applicable tax elections, rollover and earnout mechanics, and a sequenced closing checklist for the proposed acquisition of [TARGET ENTITY] ("Company") by [ACQUIROR ENTITY] ("Buyer"). The plan is designed to optimize after-tax proceeds to selling shareholders, minimize Buyer's depreciable/amortizable asset basis step-up cost, and achieve certainty of close while satisfying applicable regulatory requirements.

**Recommended Structure:** **Reverse Triangular Merger (§368(a)(2)(E)) with a §338(h)(10) election available as a toggle**, subject to final determination of (i) seller entity type and (ii) rollover quantum. A stock-deal baseline is assumed; asset-deal mechanics are preserved as a fallback toggle.

---

## SECTION 2 — STRUCTURE SELECTION ANALYSIS

### 2.1 Comparison Matrix

| Criterion | Asset Purchase | Stock Purchase | Forward Merger | Reverse Triangular Merger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Buyer basis step-up** | Full fair-value step-up | Carry-over basis (unless §338) | Carry-over (unless §338(g)) | Carry-over (unless §338(h)(10) if S-Corp target) |
| **Target tax on sale** | Ordinary + capital gain (double tax if C-Corp) | Capital gain only (single tax) | Capital gain only | Capital gain only |
| **Consent requirements** | Per-asset / per-contract assignments | Single-block stock transfer | Shareholder vote (both sides) | Target shareholder vote only |
| **Third-party consents** | Change-of-control clauses triggered | Change-of-control clauses triggered | May be triggered | Generally not triggered (shell survives) |
| **Successor liability** | Generally none assumed | Assumed by Buyer | Assumed | Assumed by surviving entity |
| **Complexity** | High (schedules, deeds, filings) | Low–Medium | Medium | Medium–High |
| **Best for** | Asset-heavy, clean IP transfers | PE platform add-ons, public companies | Strategic all-stock deals | PE buyouts of closely held targets |

### 2.2 Recommended Structure — Rationale

**Reverse Triangular Merger** is recommended based on the following:

1. **Consent minimization:** Target's existing contracts, licenses, and government permits survive by operation of law in the surviving entity. Asset assignments and novations are eliminated.
2. **Tax efficiency to sellers:** Sellers recognize long-term capital gain on merger consideration (assuming ≥12-month holding period), avoiding ordinary income characterization.
3. **§338(h)(10) toggle:** If Target is an S-Corporation or a subsidiary in a consolidated group, a joint §338(h)(10) election can convert the stock deal into a deemed asset sale for tax purposes only—giving Buyer a full fair-value asset basis step-up while sellers retain single-level tax treatment. This election must be evaluated against the incremental tax cost to sellers (ordinary income on certain asset classes) against the purchase-price premium Buyer is willing to pay for the step-up.
4. **Rollover compatibility:** Rollover equity from management can be structured as a tax-free exchange under §351 or §721 into Buyer's acquisition vehicle (NewCo HoldCo), preserving rollover participants' tax deferral on the rolled portion.

### 2.3 Asset Deal Fallback Trigger Conditions

An asset purchase structure should be substituted if any of the following conditions are confirmed:

- Target is a C-Corporation with significant net operating losses (NOLs) that do not survive a §382 ownership change analysis at acceptable levels.
- Third-party consent analysis reveals that reverse triangular merger triggers change-of-control provisions in material contracts (>15% of LTM revenue).
- Seller insists on "clean hands" with respect to successor liability for legacy environmental, product liability, or pension obligations.
- Regulatory approval requires asset carve-out (e.g., HSR remedies).

---

## SECTION 3 — TAX ELECTIONS

### 3.1 §338(h)(10) Election

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Availability** | S-Corp targets; C-Corp targets that are members of a consolidated group (joint election with common parent) |
| **Effect** | Deemed asset sale at closing date; Buyer receives fair-value tax basis in all Target assets; goodwill and §197 intangibles amortizable over 15 years |
| **Seller impact** | Gain allocated across asset classes per §1060 residual method; Class V–VII assets (customer lists, goodwill) taxed as capital gain; Class IV (inventory) as ordinary; Class I–III (cash, securities) minimal gain |
| **Buyer economics** | NPV of 15-year amortization on step-up (Buyer typically pays 10–20% purchase price premium to fund seller's incremental tax) |
| **Deadline** | Filed on Form 8023 no later than 15th day of 9th month following close |
| **Decision gate** | Parties must agree in the purchase agreement; include §338(h)(10) cooperation covenant and tax gross-up / purchase price allocation schedule as Exhibit |

### 3.2 §754 Election (Pass-Through Target / Partnership)

If Target is structured as an LLC or partnership:

- A §754 election causes the acquiring partnership to adjust the inside basis of partnership assets to reflect the purchase price paid by Buyer (§743(b) adjustment).
- Election is made on the partnership's tax return for the year of the transfer; must be included in the purchase agreement as a required covenant.
- Buyer's §743(b) step-up is allocated per §755 among partnership assets.
- **Critical:** The §754 election is entity-level and irrevocable absent IRS permission; confirm Target has not already made the election (which would benefit Buyer) or that revoking a prior election is not needed.

### 3.3 §336(e) Election

Available as an alternative to §338(h)(10) where:
- Target is a domestic C-Corp (not just S-Corp or consolidated subsidiary).
- Selling shareholder(s) hold ≥80% and make a "qualified stock disposition."
- Election is unilateral (seller only; Buyer consent not required).
- Effect mirrors §338(h)(10) for purposes of Target's asset gain recognition.

### 3.4 State & Local Tax (SALT) Elections

| Jurisdiction | Issue | Action |
|---|---|---|
| State of incorporation | Some states do not conform to §338(h)(10); separate state asset sale may be deemed to occur | Map state-by-state; include SALT step-up value in deal model |
| Apportionment | Post-close apportionment changes may affect effective state rate | Model pre- and post-close apportionment factors |
| Transfer taxes | Asset deals trigger deed transfer taxes; stock/merger deals generally exempt | Confirm exemptions in applicable states; budget for any exposure |

### 3.5 Purchase Price Allocation (§1060 / §338 Residual Method)

Allocation Schedule (to be agreed pre-close and attached as Exhibit to SPA):

| Class | Asset Category | Allocation Method |
|---|---|---|
| Class I | Cash & cash equivalents | FMV (usually book = tax) |
| Class II | Actively traded securities | FMV |
| Class III | Debt instruments, A/R | FMV |
| Class IV | Inventory | FMV |
| Class V | Other tangible assets (PP&E) | Appraisal / agreed value |
| Class VI | §197 intangibles (customer lists, IP, non-compete) | Agreed value; residual |
| Class VII | Goodwill & going concern value | Residual (remainder after Classes I–VI) |

**Binding allocation:** Both parties must use the agreed allocation; any inconsistency triggers reporting obligations under §1060(b). Attach allocation schedule as a pre-closing covenant with a dispute resolution mechanism (independent appraiser if parties cannot agree within 30 days post-close).

## SECTION 4 — ROLLOVER MECHANICS

### 4.1 Overview

Management rollover converts a portion of management's sale proceeds into equity of NewCo HoldCo (or an intermediate holding vehicle), achieving:
- **Tax deferral** for rollover participants on the rolled portion.
- **Alignment** of management incentives with Buyer's investment thesis.
- **Reduction** of cash consideration at close (lowers Buyer's equity check / debt service).

### 4.2 Recommended Rollover Vehicle

**Buyer's HoldCo LLC (taxed as partnership)** — preferred over C-Corp HoldCo because:
- Flow-through of gains/losses to management upon exit.
- Profits interest grants available as additional incentive compensation (§83(b) elections).
- No double-tax on exit if HoldCo is liquidated or sold.

### 4.3 Tax-Free Rollover Treatment (§351 / §721)

| Code Section | Applicability | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| **§351** | Rollover into C-Corp NewCo | Transferors must control ≥80% of NewCo stock immediately after exchange; no "boot" other than permitted |
| **§721** | Rollover into partnership / LLC | No 80% control test; gain not recognized on contribution of property to partnership in exchange for partnership interest; "disguised sale" rules must be respected |

**Disguised sale risk (§707):** If rollover participant receives cash or debt relief within 2 years of contributing property to the partnership, the IRS may recharacterize as a taxable sale. Structure rollover so that:
- Distribution of deal proceeds to rolling participants occurs only from Buyer-funded consideration, not from contributed assets.
- No guaranteed payments or preferred returns payable within 24 months of rollover.

### 4.4 Rollover Quantum & Negotiation Parameters

| Parameter | Typical Range | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Rollover % of management equity | 10%–30% of total consideration | 20% as anchor; negotiated up to 30% for key employees |
| Rollover form | LLC units (Class B) | Profits interest overlay for incremental upside |
| Vesting | 4-year time vest with cliff; accelerate on liquidity | 1-year cliff + pro-rata monthly thereafter |
| Anti-dilution | Broad-based weighted average | Standard |
| Drag-along / Tag-along | Pro-rata with Buyer | Standard |
| Put/Call | Put at 3× or 5 years (whichever earlier); Call at Buyer's option post-vest | Negotiate call price floor at FMV |

### 4.5 §83(b) Election

Management receiving restricted rollover units (subject to forfeiture risk) should file §83(b) elections within **30 days of grant** to:
- Lock in current FMV (likely nominal at grant) as ordinary income recognition point.
- Convert all future appreciation to capital gain.
- **Deadline is hard and non-extendable.** Prepare election forms and calendar reminder as part of closing deliverables.

---

## SECTION 5 — EARNOUT MECHANICS

### 5.1 Overview

Earnout provisions bridge valuation gaps between Buyer and Seller, providing Seller contingent consideration tied to post-close performance. They also allocate risk: Buyer pays more only if business performs.

### 5.2 Earnout Structure Parameters

| Parameter | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | 12–24 months (longer earnouts increase management distraction and dispute risk) |
| **Metric** | EBITDA (preferred over Revenue; harder to manipulate) or Gross Profit for SaaS targets (ARR / NRR) |
| **Measurement period** | Calendar year or trailing 12 months post-close |
| **Threshold / Hurdle** | Minimum performance gate before any earnout payable (e.g., 90% of Target EBITDA) |
| **Cap** | Maximum earnout cap (typically 15%–25% of base purchase price) |
| **Payment timing** | 90 days after end of measurement period; audited financials required |
| **Acceleration** | Full acceleration upon (i) Buyer-initiated termination of key management, (ii) sale of Company before earnout period ends, (iii) material breach by Buyer of operating covenants |
| **Dispute resolution** | Independent accounting firm as expert (not arbitrator) for earnout disputes; 30-day cure period |

### 5.3 Earnout Tax Treatment

| Scenario | Tax Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Seller — open transaction (rare)** | If total consideration is not reasonably ascertainable at close, seller may report on open-transaction basis (gain recognized as earnout payments received) |
| **Seller — installment method (§453)** | If earnout is contingent and subject to §453, seller reports gain ratably as payments received; dealers and accrual-method taxpayers may be ineligible |
| **Buyer** | Earnout payments are added to purchase price in the tax year paid; purchase price allocation must be updated; §338(h)(10) election allocation may need to be re-opened if earnout is treated as additional consideration |
| **Service-linked earnout risk** | If earnout is conditioned on continued employment, IRS may recharacterize as ordinary compensation (not capital gain); decouple earnout from employment continuity or use "walk-away" provisions |

**Key drafting point:** Include a **"no manipulation" covenant** obligating Buyer not to take actions that artificially reduce the earnout metric (e.g., loading SG&A into the earnout entity, changing accounting methods, diverting customers post-close).

### 5.4 Earnout Escrow / Security

- Buyer to establish an **escrow account** funded at close equal to the maximum earnout amount if Buyer's credit quality is uncertain.
- Alternatively, a **letter of credit** from Buyer's bank.
- Seller's counsel to ensure security interest is not subordinated to Buyer's senior credit facility.

## SECTION 7 — GIVE-GET ANALYSIS & TRADE PACKAGES

```
REDLINE-RATIONALE/v2

SUMMARY: The following give-gets reflect the principal economic and structural
negotiation points arising from the recommended Reverse Triangular Merger
structure with §338(h)(10) toggle, rollover equity, and earnout bridge.

GG-01: §338(h)(10) Election — Buyer pays a purchase-price premium (typically
8–15% of incremental step-up value, net-present-valued over 15-year amortization
period) in exchange for Target shareholders accepting deemed asset-sale tax
treatment, including potential ordinary income on certain asset classes.
Certainty of close: HIGH (quantifiable via tax model). Compliance: Requires
filing Form 8023 within 9-month deadline; late-filing relief available under
Rev. Proc. 2003-33 but not guaranteed.

GG-02: Rollover Equity Quantum — Seller accepts reduced cash at close (20%
of management equity rolled) in exchange for (i) continued participation in
upside at Buyer's anticipated exit multiple, (ii) §83(b) election preserving
capital gain treatment on appreciation, and (iii) Buyer granting profits interests
as additional incentive layer. Risk to Seller: illiquidity; risk to Buyer:
dilution and governance complexity.

GG-03: Earnout Bridge — Seller accepts 10–15% of total consideration in
contingent earnout payments (24-month EBITDA metric) in exchange for Buyer
accepting higher headline enterprise value. Seller receives no-manipulation
covenant, acceleration triggers, and escrow security. Buyer receives downside
protection if projected performance is not achieved. Certainty of close: MEDIUM
(earnout disputes are the single largest source of post-close litigation).

GG-04: Purchase Price Allocation — Buyer pushes allocation toward Class VI/VII
(15-year amortizable §197 intangibles and goodwill) to maximize depreciation
shield. Seller prefers maximum allocation to Class VII (capital gain goodwill)
and minimum to Class V (recapture risk on PP&E) and Class VI (ordinary income
risk on non-competes). Negotiated resolution: independent appraiser for Class V
PP&E; agreed split of Class VI vs. VII balances both parties' interests.

GG-05: Earnout Metric — Buyer prefers Revenue (simpler, harder to manipulate
through cost allocation) but accepts EBITDA in exchange for covenant restricting
Buyer's ability to change accounting methods or load expenses into earnout entity
post-close. Seller accepts EBITDA metric in exchange for defined "Earnout EBITDA"
calculation methodology attached as a closing exhibit.

TRADE-PACKAGE: Balanced Close — §338(h)(10) Step-Up with Escrow-Secured Earnout
```

## SECTION 8 — RISK REGISTER

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | §338(h)(10) election missed (9-month deadline) | Low | High | Calendar reminder; include as post-close covenant; late-filing relief available |
| R-02 | Earnout dispute / litigation | Medium | High | Tight metric definition; independent accountant expert; escrow security |
| R-03 | Disguised sale recharacterization of rollover | Medium | High | 2-year buffer; no guaranteed payments; counsel opinion |
| R-04 | State non-conformity with §338(h)(10) | Medium | Medium | SALT mapping pre-close; reserve in purchase price model |
| R-05 | Change-of-control clause triggered despite merger structure | Low-Medium | High | Contract review in diligence; obtain required consents pre-close |
| R-06 | §382 NOL limitation post-close (if C-Corp target) | Medium | Medium | §382 study pre-close; NOL value modeled at haircut |
| R-07 | §83(b) election not timely filed for rollover participants | Low | High | Track 30-day window from close; file within 48 hours of grant |
| R-08 | Purchase price allocation dispute (tax authority) | Low | Medium | Arm's-length appraisal; binding allocation agreement; consistency covenants |
